title: secp256k1-ecdlp: parallel rho on classes of six points, truncated at success 0.39

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and Q=[x]P on secp256k1 with the protected generator P, van Oorschot-Wiener parallel collision search with an r=2048 adding walk on classes {+-R, +-phi(R), +-phi^2(R)} (negation and the GLV endomorphism phi(x,y)=(beta x,y)=[lambda]), canonical representative min{x, beta x, -x-beta x} with even y, 2-cycle look-ahead, periodic fruitless-cycle detection, 2^32 batched walks and distinguished points at rate 2^-40, stopped after T=ceil(1.04*sqrt(2 ln(1/0.61) n/6)) additions (~2^126.756), recovers x with probability at least 0.39 (random-mapping prediction 0.414) using at most 2^127.313705 total target-group-operation equivalents at C=1000, charging 1 batched affine addition plus 470 instructions per step (452 measured with Callgrind on the organizer toolchain, plus inversion share and allowance), the post-budget DP tail, all trail starts, fruitless-cycle restarts (rate bounded by 2^-20 per step), DP storage, cycle checks, the step table, trail recomputation, solving and verification. Peak memory about 2^93.6 bytes; preprocessing (step table plus clearing the DP hash table) about 2^80.6 (included); nonuniform advice 0 bytes. Heuristic: the standard Pollard-rho random-mapping heuristic for r-adding walks on automorphism classes, with the 4% step slack covering walk non-randomness and fruitless-cycle losses (supported by toy experiments and the cited literature). No quantum steps.

experiments.purpose: Part 1: Verify n prime, n = 1 mod 3, phi(P)=[lambda]P and phi^2(P)=[lambda^2]P on the real generator, and recompute T, every ledger term and the rounded-up log2 W exactly. Part 2: Run the exact class walk (canonical rep, r-adding walk, 2-cycle look-ahead, restarts on fruitless cycles) on random small j=0 curves of prime order with the same budget formula T=ceil(1.04*sqrt(2 ln(1/0.61) n/6)) counting every addition; report the fraction of secrets recovered within budget. Toy scope only.
